messages:
Jia Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the console observability work tied to customer asks (FlowAI + MidMarketOps). FlowAI insists on per-route cost breakdown, and MidMarketOps wants better error analytics for canary rollouts. Can we triage what actually fits in v1?
Alex Rivera: High level: dashboards templates + tracing hook sampling + per-route cost tags are the three asks. Main constraint is storage/query cost for fine-grained cost breakdown.
Tom Blake: Agree w/ Alex. Also need to decide default trace sampling policy. High sampling = expensive. For production we should do adaptive sampling + sticky on errors.
Sophia Patel: For dashboards: propose 3 templates — "Cost by Route", "Error Spike Inspector", "Trace Flame for Hot Paths". Each template must be light-weight SQL so it hits our metrics store cheaply.
Maya Li: Customer perspective — FlowAI will only go Dedicated if they can see cost per API route and attribution to model variants. They promised this is a gating item.
Jia Chen: OK. Let's propose MVP acceptance criteria. observability-bot: Acceptance criteria draft inserted:```
- Cost-by-route dashboard: shows 7-day cost and 1h rollup; filters by model, route, customer-id
- Trace hook: captures trace id + route + model_variant + error_flag; sampling >= 100% for errors, 1% baseline for success
- Error analytics: top-10 error slices (route + error_code) with regressions alerts
- Templates available in Console UI and exportable as CSV
- Storage/retention: metrics 30d, traces 7d (configurable)
```
Alex Rivera: Implementation notes: per-route cost needs tagging at request ingress. Minor SDK change + runtime tag propagation. Cost calc job will roll-up token counts * model unit cost. Estimate: 2 engineer-weeks for tagging + 1 week for rollup and queries.
Tom Blake: Infra concerns: traces at 1% baseline across thousands of qps -> about N traces/day. We can rely on adaptive sampling but need SLO for query latency on dashboard. Also need a quota guard for heavy query exports.
Sophia Patel: UX notes: add a sample query in the template panel that shows the SQL and an "explain cost" link. That helps enterprise reviewers approve the feature.
Jia Chen: Prioritization ask: given limited cycles, do we ship partial per-route cost (rollup only, no historical drilldown) + full error analytics + basic trace hook? Or delay cost breakdown until next cycle? Thoughts?
Maya Li: FlowAI will accept rollup-only if we promise historical drilldown in Q2. They need the spend visibility now to commit.
Alex Rivera: Rollup-only reduces query complexity a lot. We can precompute hourly rollups and expose that in dashboards. That fits the 3-week sprint if we assemble a small squad.
Tom Blake: I'm +1 for rollup-only approach. We should bake a canary for tagging + fallback to aggregated mode if tagging fails. Add circuit breaker metrics.
Jia Chen: Great. Owners: Alex -> cost tagging & rollup, Sophia -> dashboard templates & UX, Tom -> trace sampling & infra SLOs, Maya -> customer sign-off.
observability-bot: Action items auto-created: [#A1] Tagging PR (Alex) due 1719090000; [#A2] Rollup job + query (Alex) due 1719176400; [#A3] Dashboard templates (Sophia) due 1719176400; [#A4] Sampling policy doc + SLO (Tom) due 1719176400; [#A5] Customer demo prep (Maya) due 1719262800
Jia Chen: Next step: short planning sync tomorrow 10am to convert items to tickets and estimate. If anyone has major objections to rollup-first, say now.
Alex Rivera: No objections. Ship rollups + alerts first.
Tom Blake: No objections. Will draft sampling policy tonight.
Sophia Patel: I'll sketch templates by EOD and post mocks.
Maya Li: I'll coordinate FlowAI expectations and get demo slot.
Jia Chen: Thanks team. I'll create the planning card and invite folks to the 10am. :thumbsup:
